  PROBLEM: `rf"^{re.escape(name)}\(\)\n\{{\n.*?\n\}}\n"` mixes a raw f-string with regex backslash escapes for braces. The `\{`/`\}` are redundant in the regex (the same brace character), and the construct depends on Python's specific handling of `\{` inside raw f-strings; the same goal is reached more clearly with `{{` and `}}` (f-string brace escapes).
  WHY: The pattern compiles and the tests pass on the current Python, so this is not a runtime defect today. The clarity cost is the only real concern; a future Python release that tightens raw f-string parsing could surface it as a `SyntaxError` that breaks every test in the file at collection time.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh: lines 540-560 (`_resolver_model_index_prepare`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The helper resolves the real index with `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index` without defensively clearing `GIT_INDEX_FILE` in the helper's own environment. If a caller (or an outer `env` block, or `GITHUB_ENV`) has set `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, the resolved `_real_index` could point to that override path; combined with the helper's `rm -f "${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}" "${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}.lock"`, this is one assignment mistake away from deleting the wrong file.
  WHY: The standard workflow does not set `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and `git rev-parse --git-path` does not generally consult it, so today's run paths are safe. The invariant is still worth pinning because every other resolver guard in this file treats its assumptions as untouchable (#5627's whole premise is that a permissive env state reintroduces a previous bug).

  Requirement: "Each attempt now gives the model a fresh copy of the captured index through `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and the script still stages and commits the accepted resolution itself." (PR description; restated in `changelog.d/5627-resolver-private-model-index.md:4`.)

  Evidence of absence: The PR adds an agents.md paragraph and a changelog fragment that describe the private-index side, but neither names the dual-index contract: the model sees `GIT_INDEX_FILE=${RUNTIME_DIR}/resolver_model_index` and the script's own `git add` after the loop must run on the real index (no `GIT_INDEX_FILE` in its env). A future edit that "simplifies" the staging step by also prefixing `GIT_INDEX_FILE=${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}` would silently reintroduce the original failure mode: the resolution would land in the private copy, `.git/MERGE_HEAD` would point to a stage that the commit never reads, and the resulting `[ai-merge-resolve]` would carry nothing. The staged-add call sites therefore need an explicit "intentionally on the real index" marker so future editors do not "unify" the wiring.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh: `_resolver_model_index_prepare` (lines 548-560) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index` honours `GIT_INDEX_FILE` if it is set in the caller's environment, resolving `_real_index` to that value instead of `.git/index`. If that value equals `RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE`, the subsequent `rm -f -- "${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}"` deletes the live repository index before `cp` tries (and fails) to read the now-missing source.
  WHY: In the normal workflow `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is unset, so this does not fire today. But the test conftest already strips `GIT_INDEX_FILE` from subprocess environments precisely because it can leak, and any future caller or workspace hook that exports it would turn this function into a live-index wipe followed by a failed `cp` and `exit 1`. The fix is one line: either `unset GIT_INDEX_FILE` before the `git rev-parse` call, or guard the `rm -f` with `[ "${_real_index}" != "${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}" ] || return 1`.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Each attempt now gives the model a fresh copy of the captured index through `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and the script still stages and commits the accepted resolution itself." (PR description, changelog.d/5627-resolver-private-model-index.md:4)
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` — `stage_resolver_touched_path_or_fail` and the post-loop `git add -u -- ...` block
  Evidence of absence: both staging sites call `git add` without `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, which correctly falls through to the real index — that is the intended behaviour. But neither the PR description, the agents.md note, nor a code comment at the staging sites calls this out as the staging contract. A future editor who "simplifies" the wiring by exporting `GIT_INDEX_FILE=${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}` to the post-loop stage would silently reintroduce the bug in a new direction (resolution staged into the private copy, real index still has unmerged entries, commit built off the real index without the staged content). A one-line comment at each staging site (`# real index: model's private copy is not used here`) would lock the contract.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
